summary: The team launched the blog with a short introduction post before the trip began.

Olivia reflected on pre-departure planning in Cambridge: communication and organization went well, but a member got too sick to take part and a bike was stolen. The team was set to start biking June 11.
learning_festival: Planned for nine schools/organizations; no details given in this post.
contacts: Ace Wheelworks, Porter Square (Cambridge, MA) - final gear checks
planning_notes: Group roles were assigned at the start but morphed over the semester as new tasks came up; expect roles to shift.
Past Spokes teams said this team was well ahead of them on planning; communication and organization were the team's main successes.
Pre-departure setbacks were a stolen bike and a member too sick to ride; the team handled them calmly.

summary: Olivia listed the fruit she had picked or tasted so far (raspberries, mulberries, black raspberries) and the lavender her host John picked and used to freshen the van.
contacts: John (host, town not stated)

summary: Day one left from the Washington Monument in DC at noon instead of 8am, rode 35 miles in heat split into three legs, and reached WarmShowers hosts Cindy and Jerry in Montclair, VA, five hours behind schedule.
slept_at: Cindy and Jerry (WarmShowers host), Montclair, VA
contacts: Cindy and Jerry, WarmShowers hosts, Montclair, VA
planning_notes: The team left at noon, not 8am, and rode in the worst heat of the day; an early start avoids that.
Breaking the day into chunks with a food stop about 12 miles in (tuna and peanut butter sandwiches) improved pacing and hydration for the later legs.
Swarm of bees on the first leg through Alexandria, VA.

summary: The team reached Montclair, VA, then averaged about 50 miles a day through Virginia, detoured from Natural Bridge to the Dinosaur Kingdom II amusement park, and prepped for its first Learning Festival in Hazard, KY.
slept_at: Cindy and Jerry (WarmShowers host), Montclair, VA (first night); other nights not stated
learning_festival: Upcoming first Learning Festival in Hazard, KY, about two days away at the time of this post.
contacts: Cindy and Jerry, WarmShowers hosts, Montclair, VA
Mark Cline, artist behind Dinosaur Kingdom II, VA
Host family in Silver Spring, MD (unnamed) who let the team stay at the start
planning_notes: Pre-trip transport: two cars carried workshop material, luggage, snacks and seven bikes from Boston to Philadelphia and Silver Spring, MD.
Virginia hills got steeper; the team averaged about 50 miles a day.
Dinosaur Kingdom II (near Natural Bridge, VA) is an amusement park the team chose as a stop instead of Natural Bridge itself.

summary: The team finished its first Learning Festival, two days at the Challenger Learning Center in Hazard, KY, and was honored at a board cookout with official Duke and Duchess of Hazard certificates.
learning_festival: Two-day festival at the Challenger Learning Center, Hazard, KY (one of 47 Challenger centers; Spokes' third year there). Students came from across Kentucky. Workshop included a four-color-theorem map-coloring activity on a US map.
contacts: Challenger Learning Center, Hazard, KY (LF host)
Challenger board members, Hazard, KY (cookout and certificates)
planning_notes: The four-color-theorem map activity worked well with kids: they colored Kentucky first because it borders an odd number of states, which is the strategy behind the theorem.

Eastern Kentucky context: coal decline and opioid addiction; officials and companies such as Bit Source (retraining laid-off miners as software engineers) stress schools adapting to the new economy. Useful framing for LF pitches.

summary: After the Hazard, KY workshops, the team faced 80 miles with about 6,000 feet of climbing and a tropical storm, so they booked an Airbnb 30 miles along the route and rode out in the rain.
slept_at: Airbnb about 30 miles along the route toward East Bernstadt, KY (town not named)
contacts: Harmony House Bed and Breakfast, Hazard, KY (team's stay before this ride)
Jamie, Challenger Learning Center, Hazard, KY (invited the team to the pool and the Thursday on the Triangle event)
planning_notes: Hazard, KY to East Bernstadt, KY is about 80 miles with about 6,000 ft of climbing over the Appalachian ridge; the team's typical 60-mile days had about 2,000 to 3,000 ft.
An 800-ft hill near Hazard took 15 to 45 minutes; riders in the lowest gear or walking was normal.
In heavy rain, spray hit at 20 mph and tight turns made descents hard; plan for wet, slow downhills.
Kentucky hills flatten into corn fields toward Illinois, then Missouri gets hilly again.
Headwinds of 10 to 15 mph on flat ground; drafting behind a leader (Thi led most of the time) helped riders at the back. Word games like Contact kept morale up.

summary: Thi recapped Days 12 to 21 from Hazard, KY to Farmington, MO: a storm-dodging 30-mile day, dogs on back roads, free bike tune-ups, host hospitality, a local TV spot, and arrival at the Farmington Learning Festival.
learning_festival: Second LF in a community workspace in Farmington, MO run by Ann Boes; kids of all ages, including a First Lego League team.

planning_notes: Day 12, Hazard to Buckhorn, KY: 30 miles, chosen to dodge a thunderstorm; hilliest day so far by Thi's account. Stayed at an Airbnb in Buckhorn.
Day 13, East Bernstadt: a bike maintenance clinic taught the Air, Brakes, Chain check before every ride.
Day 14, East Bernstadt to Columbia, KY: 85 miles, mostly uphill, with unleashed dogs on back roads. Spraying dogs with a water bottle discouraged them; hosts gave pepper spray.
Southern Performance Center (KY) tuned the bikes for free when a small front gear was giving trouble.
Columbia hosts printed detailed directions to Mammoth Cave, a good model for hosts who have ridden the route.
Days 15-16: Columbia to Mammoth Cave, KY was 65 miles; Serenity Hill B&B hosted two nights; Mammoth Cave tour is a good rest-day option.
Day 17: Mammoth Cave to Hartford, KY was 60 miles; the Twin Island Trails riverside campsite had good fishing (bluegill cooked on site).
Day 18: Hartford to Henderson, KY was 68 miles; the host arranged a local TV news segment.
Day 19: Henderson to Harrisburg, IL was 70 flat miles. The next night's host cancelled; a Harrisburg host found a floor in Murphysboro. Line up backup hosts.
Day 20: Harrisburg to Murphysboro, IL was 50 windy miles. Carbondale Cycles fixed a creaking bike for free and gave discounts on tubes and clothing.
Day 21: Murphysboro to Farmington, MO was 75 miles, with a steep climb right after crossing the IL-MO border; the hardest ride by Thi's account.

summary: The team spent four teaching days in Farmington, MO and St. Louis (about 18 teaching hours in five days), building a five-bit binary adder circuit with students.
learning_festival: Lab:Revo maker-space (volunteer-run, in a factory basement, Farmington, MO) and the St. Louis Homeschool Network at a United Methodist Church, St. Louis, MO. Circuit workshop: LED warm-up, static-electricity transistor detector, binary, three logic gates, half adder, then cascaded into a 5-bit adder (inputs up to 31) with lights for output.
contacts: Ann Boes, Lab:Revo maker-space, Farmington, MO
St. Louis Homeschool Network, St. Louis, MO
planning_notes: The circuit workshop is a strong hands-on capstone: students build a half adder and cascade them into a working 5-bit calculator. Sequence: LED, transistor detector, binary, logic gates, half adder, adder.
Informal venues (maker-spaces, homeschool networks) meant smaller groups of regular attendees than at the Challenger Center; plan for variable group sizes.
Four teaching days plus one riding day in a single week was heavy: about 18 teaching hours in five days.

summary: The team posted photos from its state-line crossings so far: Virginia-Kentucky, Kentucky-Illinois, Illinois-Missouri, Missouri-Kansas and Kansas-Colorado.

Margalit broke down the 2,250 miles so far by surface (about 1,800 paved, 150 dirt, 300 trail) and described the trails the team rode, from the Mount Vernon trail out of DC to the Katy Trail and Denver-area paths, with thorny surfaces causing many flats.
planning_notes: Katy Trail (Missouri): about 240 miles of crushed limestone rail trail across most of the state; the team rode about 220 miles of it. Flat and long, the team's favorite kind of riding.
Flint Hills Nature Trail (Kansas): rough, thorny surface. The team rode only 5 miles but got many punctures over the next 3 days; bring puncture-resistant tires or extra tubes.
A 5-mile 'Natural Earth' trail section was a thorny mess that caused 10+ punctures.
Tunnel Hill State Rail Trail (Harrisburg, IL) is 56 miles; the team rode part of it.

Denver to Fort Collins, CO: South Platte River Trail, Cherry Creek Trail and Denver-Boulder Bikeway, then bike lanes. Colorado is ranked 7th most bike-friendly state by the League of American Bicyclists.
Between Kansas and Denver there were stretches of up to 50 miles of only farms or grassland with no trails and few cars. Carry water and plan for distance.
